Order of the Ashen Rose → Rósande (B04 → Z35)

Region (English scoring-table division): Escann.

Story: high｜Mission-tree length: long｜Mission-tree update: updated in the current version｜Distinctiveness: very high｜Waiting burden: medium-high｜Early pressure: high｜Expansion capacity: high.

Identity and history

Rósande’s (Z35) only confirmed continuous predecessor is the Order of the Ashen Rose (B04). The current Mod defines B04 as a High Lorentish order with Regent Court faith, an adventurer theocracy, and capital 817; Z35 is a Rósanda-culture Regent Court monarchy with capital 817 as well. B04’s history records a 1400 adventurer-order marker and a 1431 female commander from a branch of the Ording family. Z35’s country definition retains a settled-country monarchy and adventurer-kingdom reform, describing the post-formation state rather than proving that Z35 was selectable in 1444.【Local history script】

The offline Wiki describes the Ashen Rose as an infamous order formerly based in the Duchy of Eilísin, led by Captain Maugunia of Ording into Escann against the Greentide. It then describes their settlement in South Castanor and their reform into Rósande. That later succession is historical setting, not proof that formation was complete in 1444. The short Wiki entry supplements background but does not replace current mission logic.【Wiki source】

National story and campaign line

The Ashen Rose is not a story of a redeemed order. It combines exiled knights’ military prestige, hostility toward Orcs, noble wealth, and settlement in Escann into a brutal state project. The Z35 tree begins with knights, chains, and disgraced nobles: mission text directly depicts knights capturing Orcs, chaining them to labour, lowering Orc tolerance, adding an Orcish labour modifier, and changing the product to wine.【Local narrative text】【Local script】

The formation relation is explicit: the Escann formation effect runs under limit = { tag = B04 }, executes change_tag = Z35, and runs swap_non_generic_missions = yes. This is one B04-to-Z35 tree-swap chain, not two parallel countries, and Z35 missions must not be back-projected onto B04. Before settlement, B04 must hold territory in Blade Marches, Humacvold, or Temin; afterwards Rósande expands into South Castanor, the Deepwoods, and old-kingdom inheritance.

Core mechanics

The first core is Orcish labour and plantation wine. Establishing a plantation requires the relevant mission, 100 ducats, 50 military power, an Orc population, at least ten regiments, and labour-modifier conditions. Orc-culture provinces can change culture and religion, lose 5 regiments, become wine-producing, and suffer reduced Orc tolerance.【Local script】 The Slave-Hunting Knights mission likewise links captured Orcs, a permanent labour modifier, and wine production. The wine market then requires trade share, eight provinces with labour and farm estates, and conversion of slave goods into wine; economic growth and institutional exploitation are one loop.

The second core is noble and royal restructuring. The tree moves from disgraced nobles through chains, knights, noble fashion, and the crown. Government reforms and privileges bind construction, noble loyalty, stability cost, maximum absolutism, and Orcish labour together. A selective religious turn is also possible: roughly five years after formation, an event can convert Rósande to the Infernal Court and convert the capital plus five provinces. This is a branch, not an inevitable Z35 result.【Local script】 Finally, Half-Orcs and the Deepwoods create a social tension: events acknowledge their exclusion from both societies, while later missions place forest expansion, Elven relations, and Half-Orc events alongside continued oppression.

Staged play

At the start, B04 must manage adventurer unity, neighbours, and a settlement site in Blade Marches, Humacvold, or Temin. The order is not an ordinary 1444 monarchy selectable without preparation. After formation, complete stability, noble, and Orc-labour prerequisites, then balance money and military power between war, trade, and plantations. The middle game spreads labour modifiers across farm estates and secures trade share in relevant nodes; the late game expands toward old Castanorian inheritance, the Griffin Lords, the Deepwoods, and the new kingdom order. Branches, events, waiting, and prerequisites make the campaign medium-high in waiting burden rather than impossible.

Formable country and endgame

Only B04 → Z35 is confirmed. The Z35 tree contains 35 direct mission definitions across foundation, post-settlement branches, nobles and knights, royal expansion, and final forging. The count follows the local deterministic index and is not an artificial recount. The endgame theme is to make Rósande an Escanni power through wine, noble court, and knightly force while contesting Castanorian inheritance. Routes may retain the Regent Court, turn to the Infernal Court, or alter social composition through Half-Orc and Elven content; none automatically becomes a good route.

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 90/100｜Autocracy 82/100｜Magic↔Artifice 60/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 55/100)｜Pluralism 25/100. The B04 baseline is Expansion 68, Autocracy 74, Magic↔Artifice 55, intensity 45, Pluralism 30; Z35 is Expansion 90, Autocracy 82, Magic↔Artifice 60, intensity 55, Pluralism 25.

The v2.1 value profile is evil (22/100), with a trajectory classified as branch_dependent. The five personality coordinates remain Expansion 90, Autocracy 82, Magic–Artifice direction 60, theme intensity 55, and Pluralism 25. This is a noble-led conquest state with high expansion and centralisation, a relatively limited magical narrative, and low recognition of diversity. Direction and intensity are separate measures: the intensity score of 55 describes how prominent the theme is in national play, while an optional conversion to the Infernal Court does not turn the whole country into a purely magical state. The overall value classification is Evil 22. The value assessment is Dignity 18, Public Good 35, Personhood Recognition 12, and Restraint 25, weighted at 35/25/25/15 for a rounded value of 22. Its low score comes from explicit slave-catching, chained labour, Orc enslavement, and exclusion of Half-Orcs—not from having many wars, a monarchy, or a goal of unification. The branch_dependent label records the limits of the outcomes: rejecting the Infernal Court and undertaking some construction paths does not cancel institutional slavery, while conversion, expansion, and flourishing wine production do not themselves establish a moral improvement.

This suits players who enjoy long mission trees, cavalry and wine economies, noble courts, dark alternate history, and actively shaping an oppressive institution. It is unsuitable for players seeking minority protection, low prerequisites, linear missions, or a bright knightly story.

Community experience and evidence boundary

Two player posts discuss the plantation–Orc–wine loop and the predecessor, heavy cavalry, and Deepwoods expansion. Neither states the Mod version, submods, or save modification, so neither overrides the current scripts. No dedicated Rósande body text was found in an official diary, and the Halan historical-map pages were unavailable. Missions, decisions, and mechanics therefore remain bounded by the local scripts.

Evidence details are linked in the source note below.

Original Chinese research evidence: source evidence; English translation receipt.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea groups are filled, and the ambition applies after all seven have been unlocked. Only national ideas themselves are listed: racial, government and mission rewards are excluded. A successor’s new set does not automatically stack with its predecessor’s ideas. Descriptions may recall history or portray future ideals, and do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Native English originals are reused rather than back-translating expanded Chinese localisation. Displayed effect values are inherited from the Chinese research data; any unresolved display units remain qualified, not silently corrected.

Rósande (Z35) — Rósander Ideas

Traditions: Rósander Traditions

Effects: Discipline: +5%; General cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Grape Corvee

The grape corvee does not merely refer to the practice of requiring the nobles to give up a portion of their slaves under a corvee system to work on royal lands every few months, but a complex legal and social system that codifies the idea that the Orcs are a uniquely inferior race, placed to serve their betters.

Effects: Development cost: -10%.

Idea 2: Knights Rósande

Shortly after the formation of Rósande, senior members of the Order of the Ashen Rose formed the Knights Rósande, the primary military elite of the country. Their crimson and black plate armour could be seen on the battlefields of Escann even far after it has stopped being used by other kingdoms, striking fear into Rósande's foes.

Effects: Cavalry combat ability: +15%.

Idea 3: Slave Hunters

Led by the grim and cruel members of the Royal Slave Catchers, every free person (who can't afford a substitute) is expected to join with the slave hunting militias after a certain age. Here, they learn that the whips that lash the slaves also can be used on their backs, as speed outstrips all other consideration as they run down fleeing greenskins to drag them back to captivity.

Effects: Movement speed: +15%.

Idea 4: King Grape

The rolling lands that host Rosande make for excellent vineries, a fact latched onto by the recently settled Ashen Rose. With plentiful land, resources, and a cheap source of labor, it is often said that the true king of Rosande does not sit in the palace, but rather on the vine, and King Grape demands plenty from its subjects. No political decision is made in the country that the leadership doesn't turn to the bounty of its tressels.

Effects: Production efficiency: +10%.

Idea 5: Forgotten Sons of Lorentish Nobility

The Order of the Ashen Rose was made up of lesser sons and bastards of the Lorentish upper class. With no future awaiting them in Lenecor they chose to carve a new future for themselves in Escann.

Effects: Advisor cost: -10%; Improve relations: +10%.

Idea 6: The Rosander Hero

Many tales during the Age of Witch-Kings focus on a Rósander hero (a variant of the literary Romantic Hero), a dark and brooding gentleman-type who is often at odds with the world and its affairs - and most importantly an incredibly alluring figure for the fairer sex.

Effects: Prestige: +1.

Idea 7: The Great Uprising of 1634

In July 1634 Surga's Rebellion shook the foundations of the kingdom. Almost one hundred orc slaves, in an unprecedented act, rose up under Surga, some even on horseback, and managed to kill almost sixty humans before being crushed. Reforms after led to even harsher laws, as well as demands from plantation owners and other free people for better equipped militias with more authority.

Effects: Harsh treatment cost: -15%; Maximum absolutism: +5.

Ambition: Rósander Ambition

Effects: Fort maintenance: -20%.

Order of the Ashen Rose (B04) — Lencori Ideas

Traditions: Lencori Traditions

Effects: Fort maintenance: -10%; Cavalry recruitment cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Luxury Trade

Our people are known to have more refined tastes than most, which has led to a booming trade in luxury goods in our lands.

Effects: Domestic trade power: +10%.

Idea 2: Vineyard Palaces

Contrary to popular belief, not every Lorentish nobleman owns a vineyard, but it's common enough that we've gained a reputation for producing the best wine and building lavish palaces to showcase them.

Effects: Prestige decay: -1%.

Idea 3: Romantic Chivalry

Whereas knighthood generally carries some social benefits elsewhere in Cannor, nowhere is it as culturally exalted as it is in Lencenor, where knights are seen as both legends of the battlefield and heroes of verse and song.

Effects: Cavalry combat ability: +10%.

Idea 4: Adroit Diplomacy

Our courtiers are well learned in the arts of etiquette and diplomacy, able to carouse and cajole even the crabbiest of Corvurians. Let us employ them as diplomats and impress the courts of Cannor.

Effects: Diplomatic reputation: +100%.

Idea 5: Lorentish Cuisine

It is simply a fact of life that the various regional dishes of Lorent collectively comprise the finest cuisine in all of Cannor. The other nations recognize this, and bask in our culinary superiority.

Effects: Prestige: +1.

Idea 6: Enlightened Embassies

Our courts aren't just for show: they are cultural and administrative marvels that balance pleasure with productivity. We can thus entertain more foreign ambassadors at once than most courts.

Effects: Diplomatic relations: +1.

Idea 7: Legacy of the Lilac Wars

Although we may not have been at the head of the Lorentish host that seized final victory in the Lilac Wars, the decades-long conflict has had a great influence on our armies. Wherever the Lorentish martial salute can be seen, our enemies will know of our impending victory!

Effects: Army morale: +10%.

Ambition: Lencori Ambition

Effects: National tax modifier: +10%.
